sources.entry: Predator - A predator-inspired clock screensaver for macOS

summary.one_liner: A macOS screensaver that turns your Mac into a Predator-movie-style clock, released as open source under Apache 2.0.
summary.what_it_does: Predator is a macOS screensaver (.saver bundle) that displays a clock styled after the Predator sci-fi movie. Users can customize the clock colors and switch between 12-hour and 24-hour time formats. An optional setting hides UI elements to get a more movie-accurate look. The README says the project is written in Swift and is open to bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests. The README does not describe the clock's internal rules beyond a heading that says they are "easy to grasp."
use_cases: Replace the default macOS screensaver with a sci-fi clock
Show a Predator-style digital clock on a Mac display
Customize clock colors and 12/24-hour time format on a screensaver
Install a fan-made Predator movie prop look on a Mac
how_to_run: Download the latest release of Predator from the link in the README
If macOS blocks it as from an unidentified developer, click OK, then open Security & Privacy in Preferences and choose Open Anyway
Quit and reopen System Preferences after installing or upgrading
To uninstall, right-click Predator in System Preferences and choose Delete Predator, or delete Predator.saver from /Library/Screen Savers or ~/Library/Screen Savers
notable: Optional hiding of UI elements for a movie-accurate look
caveats: Not signed by an identified developer, so Gatekeeper may block it and require manual approval
Some unzip tools can cause a 'damaged app' error; the README suggests downloading with Safari
